page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7a.4xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by the AMD EPYC 7T83 processor operating at a base frequency of 2.55 GHz under an x86_64 architecture. The instance delivers 16 dedicated vCPUs spanning 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core, alongside 32 GB of RAM. This provides a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The processor features 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache, supporting standard hardware extensions including AVX, AES-NI, VAES, and SHA-NI.

The instance does not include bundled local storage or dedicated GPU acceleration, relying on network-attached storage for persistent disk operations and operating with a 5 Gbps baseline network throughput. Standardized synthetic benchmarks align the instance within median cloud expectations, yielding a multi-core score of 8,253 in Geekbench and 21,196.32 in PassMark CPU tests. The instance also achieved 13,374 in Clang compilation and 15.82 million operations per second in Redis SET operations. However, uncached memory bandwidth represents a notable constraint, recording 23.77 GB/sec for large-block reads and 12.96 GB/sec for large-block writes.

By delivering dedicated compute cores paired with a compact memory footprint, the instance maintains resource efficiency for CPU-bound tasks where paying for surplus RAM is unnecessary. The absence of local scratch disks requires external volume planning for I/O heavy jobs. Overall, the configuration serves as a viable compute resource for tasks such as CI/CD software compilation, static web serving, decompression pipelines, and lightweight model inference.

Running at 2.55 GHz across an x86_64 architecture, it provides 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical cores paired with 32 GB of RAM, yielding a 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio. The instance features a 5 Gbps baseline network interface, 32 MB of L3 cache, and standard cryptographic instruction support. It contains zero bundled local storage and no GPU acceleration. Benchmark testing demonstrates median multi-core compute capability, scoring 21,196.32 on PassMark CPU and 8,253 in Geekbench multi-core, though uncached memory write throughput remains constrained at 12.96 GB/sec. This profile delivers cost-effective CPU resource density for workloads that require steady processing power without high memory overhead, making it functional for code compilation, static web traffic, batch pipelines, and small-model inference.
